description: Bogra Sadar is the main administrative, commercial, and educational hub of Bogra District. Situated on the banks of the historic Karatoya River, this upazila acts as the heart of North Bengal's transport network, connecting several northern districts with Dhaka. It features key healthcare institutions like Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College and Mohammad Ali Hospital, along with major commercial markets, historic landmarks like the Nawab Palace, and a booming industrial sector specializing in foundry and light engineering.

description: Formed as a separate upazila in 2003 by carving out southern parts of Sadar, Shajahanpur serves as a key strategic area housing the Majhira Cantonment. It lies directly along the N3 national highway, fostering rapid urban expansion and light industrial growth. The region's economy relies heavily on agriculture, livestock farming, and commerce tied to highway transportation services.

description: Sherpur is a historically rich upazila dating back to the Mughal period when it served as a strategic military post known as Sherpur Murcha. Today, it is famous for its thriving dairy industry, traditional sweets (Bogra Curd), and rice processing mills. Notable heritage sites include the 16th-century Kherua Mosque and the historical Bhabanipur Shakti Peeth temple complex.

description: Located in the eastern-central part of the district, Gabatali is predominantly an agricultural upazila traversed by the Ichamati River. It is famous for hosting the centuries-old Poradaha Mela, a massive cultural and fish fair held annually. The local economy is driven by paddy, potato, and vegetable farming alongside small-scale rural markets.

description: Shibganj is internationally renowned as the archaeological heartland of ancient Bengal. It houses Mahasthangarh, the ruins of Pundranagara dating back to the 3rd century BCE, along with key sites like Vasu Bihar and Bihar Hat Jami Mosque. Besides its archaeological importance, Shibganj is a major agricultural hub producing large yields of potatoes, vegetables, and paddy.

The upazila acts as a vital grain wholesale processing and distribution point connecting Naogaon and Joypurhat districts with central Bangladesh.

description: Bordering Naogaon District, Adamdighi is notable for Santahar, a major railway junction town and the site of the Santahar Silo, one of the nation's largest food grain storage complexes. The region relies heavily on railway transport commerce, rice milling, and freshwater fish cultivation.

description: Sariakandi is the largest upazila in Bogra by area, defined by the expansive Jamuna River and its numerous riverine char islands (shoals). It is famous for its scenic riverbanks like Prem Jamunar Ghat, which attract eco-tourists, while its char dwellers engage in crop farming (peppers, maize, jute) and seasonal fishing.
